title: Association between physical activity and cognitive function among community-dwelling older adults in Delhi NCR: a cross-sectional study
abstract: Age-associated decline in physical and cognitive functioning is one of the most significant health problems associated with healthy ageing. This study aimed to evaluate the association between physical activity (PA) level and cognitive functioning among the older Indian population residing in Delhi-National Capital Region (NCR), India. A cross-sectional study was conducted among community-dwelling adults aged 50-65 years using the International Physical Activity Questionnaire-Short Form (IPAQ-SF) and Montreal Cognitive Assessment (MoCA). The total number of respondents was 400 (mean age: 56.3 ± 5.8 years), with 67% female and 33% male. 70% of respondents were moderately active, with a mean MoCA score of 21.3 ± 3.8 and 77% had mild cognitive impairment. There was a significant positive correlation (r = .32, p < .01) between physical activity and cognitive function, with higher activity levels resulting in better MoCA scores. Older adults’ physical activity remains below WHO guidelines, highlighting the need for regular activity to maintain cognitive health.
